$comment: Source of truth for src/theme/tokens.generated.ts. Regenerate with `npm run tokens`; `npm run tokens:check` fails the build if the generated output drifts from this file. PROVENANCE, honestly: this file used to be an export of Figma variables, and as of the Warm Signal system it is not, the values here were authored directly and the Figma file is stale. Saying otherwise in a header is worse than having no header, because the next person to 'fix' a colour would go and edit Figma and see nothing happen. If the Figma library is rebuilt, the direction to re-establish is Figma -> this file, and this note should say so again.

source.system: Signal on Neutral, iOS system greys carry the chrome, and hue is reserved for meaning: coral is the one call to act, sage is presence, citrus is the token balance. Nothing else gets a hue. Renamed from "Warm Signal", which described a warm paper base that no longer exists, a system whose name asserts a fact about its own palette has to be renamed when that fact changes.
source.figmaStatus: CURRENT for colour, space, radius and motion. All 26 colour tokens are written into this file's "Signal on Neutral / colour" collection in both modes, and the scale and motion collections were reconciled against this file on 2026-08-23 (one real drift found and corrected in Figma: radius/sheet was still Material 3's 28). Typography has NO Figma representation at all: the file holds zero text styles and zero typography variables, so the 14 styles below exist only here. Do not read a type value out of Figma, there is nothing there to read. The direction of truth is this file -> Figma throughout, never the reverse.
source.ratiosMeasured: Every pair is measured, not copied: `npm run contrast:check` recomputes WCAG 2.1 relative luminance for all 19 foreground/background pairs in both modes and fails the build below target. That gate was written for the neutral-ramp swap, because a palette change is the one edit that can break legibility everywhere at once while every ratio in this file's notes still describes the old background. It immediately found two pre-existing failures: light text/tertiary measured 2.99:1 against white, and the dark hairline 1.08:1 against a dark card, a divider that was not there. Both fixed. 2026-09-01: dark mode base ramp replaced with WhatsApp charcoal family (#0B141A / #111B21 / #202C33); all 19 pairs re-verified, all pass. New lowest margin: dark hairline #2A3942 on #0B141A = 1.56:1 (requirement: >1.5:1).
source.material: Conforms to Material 3 where M3 is a number: state-layer opacities, the 48dp minimum target, the switch anatomy, the 28dp bottom-sheet corner. The M3 Expressive mechanisms, spring motion rather than curves, shape morphing under the finger, tonal surfaces, are implemented in src/theme/motion.ts and src/components/Pressable.tsx. Material You dynamic colour is deliberately NOT taken: it needs API 31+, so it could not be backward compatible, and in a product where coral means 'act' and sage means 'present' the wallpaper does not get a vote. Every control is drawn from these tokens rather than by a platform widget, which is what makes the rendering identical from minSdk 24 upward.

bg/base.note: Page background. Light stays iOS systemBackground white; the lists have no cards, rows sit directly on it divided by border/hairline (iMessage/WhatsApp). Dark is WhatsApp charcoal #0B141A — the base of the WhatsApp dark chat-list, a deep blue-black that places elevation above it as tonal lightening. NOT M3's #121212 (neutral grey) because a blue-tinted base makes the tonal steps more perceptible at low contrast and matches the product's chat-centric character. Explicit departure from M3's neutral-grey recommendation; docs/android-audit.md dark-theme entry. https://m3.material.io/styles/color/dark-theme (see also developer.android.com/develop/ui/views/theming/darktheme)

bg/raised.note: Cards, composer field, sheets. Light is pure white on the grouped grey (iOS layering). Dark is WhatsApp conversation-screen charcoal #111B21 — the chat window surface, one tonal step above bg/base so a sheet or card lifts without requiring an outline against the dark page

bg/sunken.note: Search field and disabled fills. Light is iOS systemGray5. Dark is WhatsApp toolbar charcoal #202C33 — the search/toolbar tint, two tonal steps above base, so an inset search field or disabled fill reads as slightly lighter (inset) rather than as a floating card

bg/hover.note: The M3 hover state layer. Light resolves between systemGray5 and systemGray4; Dark is a tonal step above bg/raised (#111B21) so a hovered row lifts gently — WhatsApp charcoal family midpoint between raised and sunken

bg/grouped.note: The page behind an inset-grouped form or settings list, a different idiom from a plain list. Light is iOS systemGroupedBackground grey so boxes have something to sit ON; Dark shares bg/base #0B141A and lets grouped boxes lift via tonal elevation (bg/raised) rather than a darker page

bg/chrome.note: Translucent navigation chrome: the docked bottom tab bar's fill, the page colour at 80-85% so the list scrolling under it shows through as a frost rather than a wall. This is the approximation of a real Gaussian blur (which needs a native BlurView dependency, deliberately not taken yet). Not a hex, so it is exempt from the contrast PAIRS list by construction; the pairs it matters for are measured against the opaque page colour it derives from. Dark value is bg/base #0B141A at 85%

bg/glass.note: Backdrop-blur surface tint (the composer dock + capsule, nav bar). More translucent than bg/chrome so the RenderEffect frost of the transcript actually shows through instead of reading as a white plate. Used only as a BlurView overlayColor, never a plain fill.

bg/pressed.note: The pressed state layer under a secondary button. Light is iOS systemGray4; Dark is WhatsApp charcoal #2A3942 — three tonal steps above base, a visibly deeper press than hover, matching the WhatsApp divider/selected-row tint

bg/selected.note: The full-bleed table-cell selection fill: the whole cell flashes this colour under the finger. Light is iOS systemGray4; Dark is a mid-step between bg/raised and bg/hover in the WhatsApp charcoal family so a selected row lifts distinguishably off the page

bg/inverse.note: Primary button. iOS off-black rather than #000 in light mode, so a full-width fill is a surface and not a hole. Dark mode flips to WhatsApp primary text #E9EDEF — the lightest value in the charcoal palette, which carries dark ink text at 14.6:1 (AAA)

bg/scrim.note: Material 3 scrim role for modal, menu, sheet and guided-tour backdrops. It stays black in both modes; bg/inverse is a content surface and becomes light in dark mode, which previously turned every overlay into a white veil. M3 applies the scrim role beneath elevated modal surfaces at 32% opacity. https://m3.material.io/styles/elevation/applying-elevation

bg/accent.note: ACCENT, coral.9. Marks and fills only. Measures 3.4:1 against white, so it must NEVER sit under small white text; that is what bg/accentStrong is for

bg/accentStrong.note: ACCENT, coral.10, the text-safe step. The user's own message bubble and the unread count. Light mode is a deep coral carrying white at 5.2:1; dark mode inverts to a light coral carrying ink at 6.3:1, because a deep fill on a dark page is a bubble you cannot find

bg/positive.note: The one calm band, 'how was talking to Ada?', availability on

bg/token.note: Lime/citrus mid wallet. Talk time between 10 min and 1 hour. Measures 1.3:1 as a fill, so only as a filled chip with ink on it

bg/tokenHealthy.note: Deep green wallet when ≥1 hour of talk time remains at the chat rate

bg/tokenCritical.note: Red wallet when under 10 minutes of talk time remain. Dark stays a deep red so white numeral clears 4.5:1. Distinct from coral accent so scarcity is not confused with act

text/primary.note: iOS label in light; WhatsApp primary text #E9EDEF in dark. Off-black in light for the same reason bg/inverse is; the WhatsApp charcoal value is the lightest surface in that family, 17.1:1 on bg/base #0B141A (AAA). Both are cool-neutral: no warm channel, so they cannot read as cream

text/secondary.note: Taglines, timestamps, previews. Light darkened from old warm brown to clear 4.5:1 on both grouped grey and white. Dark is WhatsApp secondary text #8696A0: 6.05:1 on bg/base #0B141A (AA), distinctly cooler than primary

text/tertiary.note: Receipts and relative times. Light raised until it clears 3:1 on white (old warm value was 2.99:1). Dark is a dimmer WhatsApp charcoal step #667D8A: 4.28:1 on bg/base #0B141A, well above the 3:1 minimum for informational text

text/muted.note: Fuse .gray for a COMPLETED or upcoming onboarding step — enumerated but receding. This IS SwiftUI Color.gray (iOS systemGray #8E8E93), verified against Step.swift where collapsed rows are .foregroundStyle(.gray); a lighter value (#AEAEB2) was tried on 2026-09-03 and looked washed out, so it is held at Fuse's exact grey (Amit). Deliberately below AA body contrast: it is a de-emphasised checklist label, not reading copy, matching the source. Never for text a user must read.

text/accent.note: ACCENT, low-balance count, accent text on a tint

text/onAccent.note: Label on bg/accentStrong, and it flips: white on the light-mode deep coral, ink on the dark-mode light coral. Both measured above 5:1

text/onInverse.note: Label on the primary button. Light: white on iOS off-black. Dark: ink on #E9EDEF (the light WhatsApp inverse surface), 14.6:1 (AAA)

text/token.note: The balance numeral on bg/token (lime mid state)

text/onTokenStrong.note: Numeral on bg/tokenHealthy and bg/tokenCritical — white on both modes so deep green/red fills stay readable

border/hairline.note: Row separators, now load-bearing rather than decorative. iOS opaqueSeparator in light. Light was #E5E5EA, which was tuned against white CARDS on a grey page; on a white page #E5E5EA measured 1.30:1 — the same invisible divider the old dark value was fixed for. Same failure, same fix, other mode. Dark is WhatsApp charcoal divider #2A3942: 1.56:1 on bg/base #0B141A, above the 1.5:1 minimum for hairline separators

border/strong.note: Input and toggle outlines, iOS systemGray3/systemGray in light. Dark is WhatsApp charcoal #374D5A — a mid-step above the hairline divider, used for field borders and toggle tracks

state/available.note: Presence dot. 3.7:1 against bg/base, which a dot needs and the softer sage did not have

state/danger.note: Destructive actions and failure notices. A deep garnet rather than a red, because a red next to a coral accent is two signals the eye cannot separate

mark/talk.note: Carousel mark. The reference pairs every carousel word with its own full-colour pictogram rather than repeating one, which is what stops the glyph reading as decoration. Our icons are line marks, so colour is what carries that per-word identity instead of artwork. One value for both modes: each clears 3:1 against white AND black, so WCAG 1.4.11 holds on either page without a second set. These are the only colours outside the accent allowed to be decorative-adjacent, and they are confined to this one component.

space.$note: Material 3 spacing tokens, base space100 = 8: hair=space25 (2), 2xs=space50 (4), xs=space100 (8), sm=space150 (12), md=space200 (16), lg=space250 (20), xl=space300 (24), 2xl=space400 (32), 3xl=space500 (40), 4xl=space600 (48), 5xl=space700 (56), 6xl=space800 (64). https://m3.material.io/foundations/layout/understanding-layout/spacing. Every value is a multiple of 2; every value from xs up is a multiple of 4. Spacing is NOT scaled with font size (M3 preserves spacing at 200% text scale, so a row grows by its text, never by its padding), and padding/gaps live on the parent. THE 16/20/24 RULE: md (16) is the compact-window body margin and the default screen edge; xl (24) is the medium-window margin and the inset of every Sheet's content (Sheet pads xl, so a child that pads again double-pads); lg (20) is kept ONLY where a surface already measured it — the sign-in family edge (Auth/Welcome/ProfileSetup/PolicyGate/ProviderStatus and App's fatal screen), card interiors (Recharge balance, Provider detail sections, Payment success), the HomeTour tooltip, PaperMenu, DayDivider, ChatStartHint, Button's label pad, and vertical rhythm on a handful of screens. New screens use md at the edge and xl inside a sheet; they do not reach for lg. hair (2) is the one sub-4 step, for the optical nudges that used to be raw 1/2/3 literals. 4xl/5xl/6xl are the checklist-to-control and section gaps that SOURCE_METRICS.formGap had to name because the scale stopped at 40; SOURCE_METRICS stays as the record of the measured source, and formGap === space['6xl'].

layout.$note: Component container heights that were module constants, so a row or bar height changes in one place. Lists: M3 list item one/two/three-line containers are 56/72/88 (https://m3.material.io/components/lists/specs); a row sets minHeight to one of these and lets its text grow it. Toolbar: the docked bottom bar is an M3 Expressive floating toolbar, not a navigation bar — 'By default all toolbars are 64dp high ... minimum outside padding of 16dp' (https://m3.material.io/components/toolbars/specs); the M3 baseline 80dp navigation bar is no longer recommended and is deliberately not used. 64 is not arbitrary: it equals space.xs + interaction.minTarget + space.xs, and a test asserts that so the bar's own padding cannot drift from its declared height. App bars: 64 small, 112 medium, 128 medium-with-subtitle (https://m3.material.io/components/top-app-bar/specs); search bar 56 (https://m3.material.io/components/search/specs). The 48dp minimum touch target stays in interaction.minTarget, not here. FlashList item estimates are derived in their components from these plus the type ladder, never typed as a bare number.

radius.$note: pressButton/pressCard/pressSend are the morph targets, kept for the Material press model that Android still uses. `field` is 10, which is the iOS search field, OTP segment and standard filled-button radius; `alert` is 14, UIAlertController's. `sheet` is 28, Material 3's specified bottom-sheet corner — M3 Paper is the product choice for every overlay (user 2026-08-30), not UISheet's 10. `screen` stays for full-screen surfaces. `tail` has no consumer any more: it was the tight corner on a message bubble's speaker side, and the chat restyle made both bubbles symmetric at 18 so fill and side carry the speaker alone. Kept rather than deleted because a tail is the obvious thing to want back, and 5 is the number that was measured to work. `bubble` is 22, the message bubble, raised from the hardcoded 18 so that a 240x180 image inset 3dp inside it gets a concentric inner radius of 19: that concentricity is the whole reason for the raise, and it is what makes a picture read as inside the bubble rather than pasted onto it. 22 and not 24 because at 22 with 16pt padding a corner-adjacent glyph still clears the curve and at 24 it does not; `xl` is there if it is ever wanted louder. `thread` is 24, the inbox conversation bubble, which can take the larger corner because it is 72pt tall rather than a line of text.

motion.$note: Springs are declared as the physical triplet (damping / stiffness / mass) rather than perceptually, because that is the only form BOTH consumers accept: withSpring takes it, and so do Reanimated's layout-animation builders via .springify().damping().stiffness().mass(). The perceptual dampingRatio is derived from these by the generator, c / (2*sqrt(k*m)), so the documented ratio can never drift from the physics actually running. Nothing positional is ever animated with a duration curve.

snap.note: Taps, chips, toggles. Just under critically damped (ratio 0.93), a hint of life with no visible wobble, settling in about 220ms

smooth.note: Sheets, screens, layout shifts. Critically damped on purpose (ratio 1.01): a bottom sheet that overshoots looks broken rather than lively

bounce.note: THE SIGNATURE MOMENT ONLY, the send. Ratio 0.59, so it visibly overshoots once and settles. Reserved so that it means something

gentle.note: Entrances and staggered cascades. Ratio 0.85, arrives with weight, does not bounce

rest.note: Settle thresholds. Reanimated's defaults let a spring hang around a pixel off for a few frames; tightening them is what makes a press feel like it ends

decay.note: Velocity handoff after a drag, a flung sheet keeps going at the speed the finger left it. This is the single largest difference between an animation and a physical interface

gesture.note: A sheet dismisses when dragged past 28% of its height OR flung faster than 800 px/s. Distance alone punishes a fast flick; velocity alone punishes a slow deliberate drag

press.note: Press scales. send squashes non-uniformly, the Y scale is what reads as weight rather than as a shrink. `row` is 0.99 rather than card's 0.975 on purpose: a flat row has no edge of its own, so a visible scale makes it look like it is peeling off the page instead of being pressed into it. `busy` is the only value here that is reasoned rather than measured: the Fuse clip says the pill compresses while its label narrates but not by how much. It is gentler than every transient press because it is HELD for the length of a network request rather than for the ~220ms a finger is down, and at button's 0.96 a held compression stops reading as pressed and starts reading as the wrong size. Same argument as row's 0.99 against card's 0.975

stagger.note: Per-item entrance delay. Above ~60ms a list stops feeling like one object arriving and starts feeling like items queueing

duration.note: Opacity and colour only. `spinnerCycle` is the period of one full revolution of the eight-spoke iOS activity indicator: UIKit runs twelve spokes at about 1s, and eight spokes need to be quicker or the gap between the brightest and dimmest spoke reads as a stutter rather than a rotation. instant is under the 100-120ms threshold where feedback stops feeling attached to the finger. accentShift, stepPromote and carouselDwell are measured, not chosen: all three come from frame-stepping the Fuse onboarding clip at 111ms per sample (see design/references/motion-system.md). The pairing of the first two is the point: the step label promotes in 150ms while the accent behind it takes 220ms to interpolate, so the content lands before its colour does and the screen never feels like it is sliding. carouselDwell is how long a focused word holds before the next one takes over; it is deliberately NOT written as breath / 4, which is 1050 and close enough to look like the same number. They are unrelated: one is a slogan cadence, the other is the typing dots' cycle, and coupling them would mean retuning the dots silently retimes onboarding

opacity.note: Two numbers rather than one, because the jobs differ. A carousel neighbour must be present as shape and absent as information: you should see that there are three lines without being able to read the other two, so 10%. An inactive stepper label must stay READABLE: it tells you what is coming and what you have done, so 25%. Both measured off the Fuse clip. Neither is a colour, so scripts/check-contrast.mjs cannot see them, and neither is a contrast claim: anything an opacity hides has to be duplicated for a screen reader

m3.$note: Material 3 screen/surface transition physics, adopted 2026-09-02 for the app-wide hybrid (ADR: motion-system.md 'Screen transitions'). Springs here are the STANDARD scheme, https://m3.material.io/styles/motion/overview/specs. UNLIKE the four springs above, these are authored as {dampingRatio, stiffness} because that is how M3 publishes them; the generator (m3Springs) converts each to the physical triplet damping=2*ratio*sqrt(stiffness*mass), mass=1, because Reanimated's withSpring silently switches to a duration parameterisation the moment a dampingRatio key is present and ignores stiffness (node_modules/react-native-reanimated/.../spring/spring.js). The EXPRESSIVE scheme (visible overshoot on spatial) is deliberately not adopted: the M3 transitions doc says common transitions should not use bouncy springs. Spatial springs move/resize; effects springs carry opacity and colour. Easing curves are the legacy emphasized set, still specified by the transition-patterns doc for enter/exit; the path-based 'emphasized' curve has no single cubic-bezier form so it is omitted rather than approximated. Durations are the M3 tokens this app actually uses.

spatialFast.note: Small fast components: menu expand, nav indicator

easing.note: M3 easing-and-duration doc. Decelerate for entering (element arrives and slows into place), accelerate for exiting (element speeds up as it leaves), standard for simple in-place changes. The 'emphasized' set is the M3 default for the largest, most expressive transitions. `decelerate` is NOT M3: it is a cubic ease-out, the curve Android's DecelerateInterpolator(1.5f) draws (1-(1-t)^3), which is what Telegram runs its 150ms fragment push/pop on (ActionBarLayout.java:614, :1873). It exists because emphasized-decelerate is ~70% complete 35ms in, so over a 150ms screen fade it reads as a cut (frame-stepped 2026-09-02: the fade finished in two frames); the cubic-out is ~35% at the same point and reads as a movement. Used only by the screen push/pop; everything else keeps the M3 curves.

duration.note: M3 duration tokens actually used by the transition builders: short for exits, screen fades and top-level fades, medium reserved for larger surfaces, long reserved. https://m3.material.io/styles/motion/easing-and-duration/tokens-specs. short3 (150) is the screen push/pop fade: Telegram Android runs its whole fragment transition in 150ms (ActionBarLayout.java:1830, DecelerateInterpolator(1.5f) at :1873) and that snap is the feel this app is measured against; M3's medium2 (300) read as sluggish on device 2026-09-02.

distance.note: Forward/back slide offset in dp for the fade-through pattern. M3 does not publish a dp for the hierarchical slide. 48 is Telegram Android's: the incoming fragment translates dp(48)*(1-t) under an alpha 0->1 (ActionBarLayout.java:1893, :1877) and the outgoing one mirrors it on pop (:1899-1907). Measured, not chosen; 24 was tried first and read as a wobble rather than a movement. A short slide under an opacity change, never a full-width push.

typography.$note: Geist (OFL, Vercel), bundled as static faces, with one exception named below. Every style names its own face rather than setting fontWeight: on Android a fontFamily plus a fontWeight makes the platform synthesise a weight it already has, which smears the letterforms. assets/fonts is the only copy; Gradle mounts it. The sizes and leading are the iOS text-style ladder rather than Material's. The exception is `wordmark` (Titan One). Geist digits are tabular by design, so the `tabular` flag on numeral tokens is honest.

wordmark.note: The word Pappal in the home nav strip, and nothing else. Titan One (SIL OFL 1.1, Rodrigo Fuenzalida, reserved name 'Titan') is the playful heavy display face Amit asked for (wave-3 #8), replacing Lilita One. Its own token rather than displayLarge with the family swapped, so a screen title stays Geist and does not silently inherit a display face. One weight only, so there is nothing here for Android to synthesise.

displayLarge.note: iOS largeTitle adapted, 30/37. Screen titles. Positive tracking, because a large title on iOS is set open, not solid. Reduced from 34 to ease onboarding density (user feedback)

displaySmall.note: iOS title1 adapted, 26/32. The inbox and directory hero. Reduced from 28 alongside displayLarge

titleMedium.note: iOS title2, 22/28. Sheet titles, provider name in the empty state

headline.note: iOS headline, 17 semibold/22. The nav-bar inline title, a list row's name, a filled button's label. There was no 17-semibold style before this, which is why every nav title in the app was 15 and read two points small

bodyLarge.note: iOS body, 17/22. Message text. The workhorse

bodyMedium.note: Composer input and sheet body. Between iOS body and callout

subhead.note: iOS subhead, 15/20. List previews and timestamps. iOS jumps 13 to 15 with nothing between, which is why captionRegular moved to 13 rather than staying at 14

labelMedium.note: Chips and starters. Buttons moved to headline

captionRegular.note: iOS footnote, 13/18. Taglines, notices, section footers

captionSmall.note: Timestamps and rail labels only. Never body copy

numeralMedium.note: The token balance. Tabular so the count does not shift the pill as it falls. Geist digits are tabular by design (monospace-inspired, uniform advances), so this flag is honest.

card.note: White cards on warm paper. Almost nothing, the colour difference does the lifting, the shadow only stops the edge dying

composer.note: Composer pill floating over the transcript

sheet.note: Bottom sheets rising over the screen

interaction.$note: Material 3 state-layer opacities, and the 48dp minimum touch target from the Android accessibility guidelines that M3 restates. The state layer is an overlay in the surface's ON colour at these opacities, it is what makes an M3 control respond even when its shape does not move, and it is the half of M3's interaction model that a scale-only press animation leaves out. Targets are met by hitSlop rather than by inflating the visual: M3's own icon buttons are a 40dp visual inside a 48dp target. `scrim` is the modal dimming behind sheets, menus and the spotlight card; M3 specifies 32% but this app was tuned to 0.4 and unifies there (the menu was 0.45). `scrimFocus` (0.54) is the deeper dim behind the HomeTour coach-marks, a focus device rather than a modal, kept separate on purpose.

toggle.$note: Material 3 switch anatomy, to the dp. The thumb growing from 16 to 24 when selected, and to 28 while held, is the detail that makes an M3 switch feel like an M3 switch, and it is the reason this is a component rather than the platform Switch: React Native's cannot express it, and on Android it renders the OEM's own colours regardless of any theme we set.
